story.yesterday: Cloud and SaaS costs were reviewed independently, obscuring the total cost and dependency impact of the digital-commerce estate.
story.today: Certified evidence connects $214M of technology investment to 340 business services across 42 countries.
story.risk: Checkout services depend on two end-of-support technologies and one concentrated payment vendor; delay increases peak-season continuity risk.
story.recommendation: Approve the phased checkout modernization and consolidate 38 overlapping SaaS subscriptions, subject to the documented service migration controls.
story.business_outcome: The governed plan protects checkout continuity and identifies $12.4M of annual opportunity without presenting it as realized value.
story.action: CIO and CFO review investment option NXR-INV-204; the Risk Committee confirms migration controls before approval.

journeys.title: Technology investment
journeys.change: Checkout growth has outpaced the resilience of two end-of-support platform components.
journeys.impact: A peak-period disruption threatens digital revenue and customer trust across 42 countries.
journeys.recommendation: Approve an $8.2M phased modernization with explicit migration controls and outcome checkpoints.
journeys.evidence: 94% synthetic evidence coverage; architecture dependencies, service health, cost baseline, and scenario assumptions are linked.
journeys.next_step: CIO sponsors the option; CFO validates the baseline; Risk Committee confirms controls.

journeys.title: Portfolio rationalization
journeys.change: Collaboration and analytics capabilities overlap across 38 SaaS subscriptions.
journeys.impact: Duplicate contracts dilute buying power, increase support burden, and obscure ownership.
journeys.recommendation: Consolidate the overlapping portfolio through controlled renewal and migration waves.
journeys.evidence: 96% synthetic evidence coverage; contracts, usage, owners, services, and renewal timing are connected.
journeys.next_step: CFO assigns benefit ownership; CIO confirms service migration; procurement sequences renewals.

journeys.title: Executive technology risk
journeys.change: Payments Authorization depends materially on one provider and has no certified financial-loss estimate.
journeys.impact: Concentration can interrupt a revenue-critical service; financial impact remains UNKNOWN until certified.
journeys.recommendation: Establish a secondary route and test failover without fabricating an uncertified loss value.
journeys.evidence: 89% synthetic evidence coverage; provider dependency, service criticality, controls, and residual unknowns are explicit.
journeys.next_step: Risk Committee accepts or mitigates the exposure; Operations rehearses failover; Finance certifies impact when evidence exists.
